title: Minimal enclosing balls via geodesics
summary: Algorithms for minimal enclosing ball problems are often geometric in nature. To highlight the metric ingredients underlying their efficiency, we focus here on a particularly simple geodesic-based method. A recent subgradient-based study proved a complexity result for this method in the broad setting of geodesic spaces of nonpositive curvature. We present a simpler, intuitive and self-contained complexity analysis in that setting, which also improves the convergence rate. We furthermore derive the first complexity result for the algorithm on geodesic spaces with curvature bounded above.
